articles.title: China and Russia are redrawing Arctic trade. Can Europe fight back?
articles.summary: For Moscow, the route offers an opportunity to redirect energy exports toward Asia as Western sanctions constrain its access to European markets, said industry watchers whom CNBC spoke to. On the other hand, it provides Beijing another trade artery that could reduce reliance on traditional maritime chokepoints.

articles.title: Bank of Japan is expected to hold rates this week — but stay hawkish: CNBC survey
articles.summary: Japan's core inflation, excluding fresh foods, for September rose 2.1% from a year earlier, reaching its highest this year as a weak yen raises import costs and elevated energy costs feed through to higher prices, even as government subsidies absorb rising costs of energy for consumers.

articles.title: From Wall Street to Silicon Valley, Anthropic IPO poised to have massive 'trickle-down effect'
articles.summary: Anthropic's IPO filing on Monday puts the Claude creator in position to pursue what could be the largest initial stock offering in history. Meanwhile, the stock market is showing signs of jitters on the AI trade. David Trainer, CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, wrote in a report last month that the AI boom has been built on the view that cheap credit and access to the capital markets will be "readily available." articles.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as AI leads to efficiency push
articles.summary: Microsoft said Monday that it's offering buyouts to a wide swath of employees as it strives to balance a costly artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out with capital efficiency. Microsoft has been ramping up spending on data centers to accommodate high AI computing demand, supplying cloud services to Anthropic, OpenAI and a slew of other companies.

articles.title: Meta, SpaceX, Anthropic stoke the AI funding frenzy. What it means for our stocks
articles.summary: The AI funding window is closing, and everyone wants a seat on the train. Meta announced plans to raise as much as $95 billion in three steps: first, an additional $22.5 billion worth of Class A common (what we and most investors currently own) priced at $642.62 per share; another $12.5 billion of preferred shares; and $60 billion no sooner than next year via an at-the-market offering for Class C shares.

articles.title: Prediction market traders say an Anthropic IPO is near-certain this year after company filed with SEC
articles.summary: Speculators on prediction market platform Kalshi place 95% odds that the artificial intelligence giant officially announces an initial public offering by the end of 2026. Kalshi defines officially announcing an IPO as either the Securities and Exchange Commission declaring an S-1 effective, a priced IPO or an exchange assigning a ticker to a stock. The Anthropic S-1 envisions a Nasdaq Stock Market ticker symbol of "ANT." Anthropic is aiming to start trading the week of Nov.

articles.title: Federal Reserve is likely to hold interest rates steady in October. Here's what that means for consumers
articles.summary: The Federal Reserve is expected to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming October meeting — even as higher energy costs complicate the inflation outlook and put additional pressure on household budgets. But fed funds futures last priced in less than a 10% chance the central bank will raise rates by another quarter point at its meeting this week, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.
